title: MATLAB repository: interconnections first, then one function at a time
subtitle: Use case walkthrough. Numbers from tools/golden_path.py on example-system/matlab-repo/
footer: Synthetic MATLAB repository. No customer data.

slides.title: One script is easy; the repository is the problem
bullets: Hundreds or thousands of .m files: scripts, functions, +packages, @classes, private/ folders
The cost is in interconnections: who calls what, through which path, and what is dynamic
Toolbox calls and shadowed built-ins decide what can leave MATLAB at all
Goal: document the repository and migrate it without feeding the whole codebase to an agent each step
No MATLAB licence needed for discovery; vectors from the original are needed for proof

slides.title: The lane, step by step
rows: entry points, toolbox and workspace boundaries, dynamic calls, order
one bounded pack per unit; manifest with bytes and tokens

slides.title: How names are resolved
slides.left_title: In MATLAB's order, as far as text allows
left: local function -> private/ -> function in tree -> frozen core list -> frozen toolbox lists
+package and @class membership from the folder, classdef methods from the file
Duplicates are marked ambiguous, never guessed
Shadowed built-ins and workspace inputs are reported per file
slides.right_title: What stays unknown, and is said so
right: eval / evalin / feval / str2func / cellfun targets: listed as dynamic
Numeric behaviour: only vectors + bench_compare.py prove that

slides.title: Bounded packs instead of the whole repository
bullets: One Markdown pack per backlog unit: source, direct dependencies, callers, open questions, boundaries
Budget per pack (default 8000 tokens est.); dependencies are trimmed before source, truncation is marked
Manifest records bytes and estimated tokens per pack so token use is visible before any agent runs
Each pack ends with a result contract: id, status, target, evidence files, blocked_on
Leaf-first order: dependencies migrate before their callers

slides.note: /matlab-to-code does one function or model at a time; /repo-discovery tells it which one and in what order.

slides.text: Map the repository once, migrate one function at a time, prove each on the owner's vectors, and let the tracker carry the status.
